findings.title: countWaveWork's doc comment contradicts its own code for a nil index
findings.detail: The comment on countWaveWork (facts.go:201-208) says: "A nil index (unreadable or unparsable) leaves both counts at zero, which is all the close could grade from it anyway." The code does not do that: `tasks++` runs unconditionally per pending task before the `if idx == nil { continue }` check (line 215-218), and the trailing `if st.Config.Review.Tasks { f.Wave.ReviewTasks = tasks }` (lines 223-225) is not gated on idx at all. So when idx is nil, VerifyCommands is 0 but ReviewTasks is still set to the pending-task count whenever review.tasks is on — not zero. This also contradicts the wave's own task brief, which states the intended behaviour as "0 for both when idx is nil". The WaveFacts.ReviewTasks doc comment in internal/decide/decide.go:156-159 ("all of them when review.tasks is on and none of them when it is off") likewise makes no exception for a nil index, reinforcing the same wrong invariant. Either the comment needs to state the real behaviour, or the code needs to match the documented/spec'd one.
